dish: Nankotsu sōki soba (soft-bone pork rib Okinawa soba) on house-made whole-wheat noodles
n: Yuunami Sakashita (自家製生麺 ゆうなみ 坂下店)
address: Terrace Sakashita 1F, 301-15 Matsukawa, Naha, Okinawa, Japan
w: A local Okinawa-soba shop whose house-made fresh noodles are blended with whole-wheat flour. You can pick thin, flat or mugwort noodles for the signature nankotsu sōki soba, and the pork-and-bonito broth is rich enough to drink to the last drop. Readers voted it into the Okinawa Times 2023 '900 noodle lovers pick' Okinawa-soba ranking (southern edition).

dish: Sanmai-niku soba (pork-belly Okinawa soba) in a two-day pork-bone, bonito, kombu and vegetable broth
n: Soba-dokoro Kikuya, Oroku (そば処 きくや)
w: A red-tiled house next to the owner's home, about five minutes by car from Naha Airport. The light broth of pork bone, bonito, kombu and vegetables is simmered for two days. The menu has sanmai-niku soba, yushi-tōfu soba and black-sugar zenzai, and it closes when sold out (around 3 pm). It was picked in the Okinawa Times 2023 reader poll of Okinawa-soba shops (southern edition).

dish: Gōyā chanpurū, tebichi and sōki-ni with nightly min'yō folk-song live music
n: Okinawa Jiryōri Angama, Kokusai-dōri (沖縄地料理 あんがま)
w: An Okinawan-cuisine and folk-song restaurant just inside the south entrance of Kokusai-dōri. The entrance is built like a red-tiled, stone-walled house and is topped by a giant mask from Ishigaki's Angama Bon festival. The menu has about 60 dishes made with island vegetables, pork and local seafood, including gōyā chanpurū, tebichi and sōki-ni, plus four set courses. Min'yō singers play every night in the third-floor hall.

dish: Okinawa soba and chanpurū set meals (lunch) with nightly sanshin shima-uta live music
n: Shima-uta to Jiryōri Tubarama, Kokusai-dōri (島唄と地料理 とぅばらーま)
w: An Okinawan-cuisine restaurant on Kokusai-dōri, a one-minute walk from Makishi Station, with an interior that recreates a pre-war Okinawan townscape. Lunch is Okinawa soba and chanpurū set meals, and sanshin shima-uta (island-song) bands play every night. OTV Okitive featured it for blending tradition with modern twists such as an Okinawan-style fried rice.

dish: Breads made with Okinawan milk and eggs, and the 'Ryūkyū king's shokupan' (琉球国王の食パン) sold at Shikinaen
n: Imai Pan, Maji (いまいパン 真地本店)
w: A neighbourhood boulangerie five minutes' walk from the Shikinaen World Heritage garden. About 80 kinds of bread fill the small shop, and owner Yōsuke Imai bakes from 5 am through the day using local ingredients such as Tamagusuku Farm milk from Nanjō and Haebaru eggs. With the Maji residents' association it also runs 'Ōchō Shokupan Shikinaen', which sells a premium 'Ryūkyū king's' loaf at the garden entrance. Okinawa Times reported on that loaf.
